{{DISPLAYTITLE:dGamer}}
'''''dGamer''''' was an independent online magazine for [[Decipher]] gamers, edited and published by [[Josh Radke]].<ref name="dgamer-fp">[http://dgamer.red84.com/ dGamer - A Magazine for DECIPHER Gamers], dgamer.red84.com (23 February 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050223115202/http://dgamer.red84.com/ Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="tfn-dgamer">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Star_Wars_CCG_Covered_in_New_Decipher_Online_Magazine_89921.asp Star Wars CCG Covered in New Decipher Online Magazine], TheForce.Net (28 February 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050308013433/http://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Star_Wars_CCG_Covered_in_New_Decipher_Online_Magazine_89921.asp Internet Archive]</ref> Its site called it "A Magazine for DECIPHER Gamers" and stated that it was "not sponsored or endorsed by Decipher".<ref name="dgamer-fp" /> It covered all of Decipher's games, including the Star Wars CCG, with Star Wars CCG game updates written by Advocates of the [[Players Committee]] and analysis articles and decks using the latest virtual cards.<ref name="tfn-dgamer" />

== Issue 1 ==

The first issue, dated January/February 2005, was a free PDF download from the magazine's site.<ref name="dgamer-fp" /><ref name="tfn-dgamer" /><ref name="pc-dl10-08">[http://www.swccgpc.com/downloads/category.php?id=10 Downloads: Player Articles and Newsletters], swccgpc.com (13 October 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081013105749/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/downloads/category.php?id=10 Internet Archive]</ref> It included a "State of the Game" article by PC Advocate [[Kevin Brownell]] and an overview by [[Tim Simon]] of the tournament environment since the release of [[Virtual Set 8]], with a look at popular decks and new virtual cards.<ref name="tfn-dgamer" /> On 24 September 2008 the Players Committee added "dGamer – Issue 1" to the Player Articles and Newsletters category of the download library on [[swccgpc.com]], as a "Decipher based newsletter from Josh Radke. January / February 2005".<ref name="pc-dl10-08" />

== Contributors and departments ==

In February 2005 the magazine's site listed Josh Radke as editor and these contributors: Paul Abbamondi, [[Justin Beal]], [[Kevin Brownell]], Jonathan Bruser, Walter Calaza, [[Jim Colson]], Xavier Davis, Tony Grain, Matt Kirk, Jason Kopka, Josh Lecker, Darren Martin, Brian Mendus, Oren Meyer, [[Tim Simon]], Shawn Sullivan, Fernando Weiss and Michael Wistrand.<ref name="dgamer-fp" />

Its departments were Reader Feedback, Brick & Mortar, Basic Training, News Deciphering, Fragments from the Rim, Gold Box, thgisdniH, Perfect Mode, The Director's Chair and CCG Index.<ref name="dgamer-fp" />

== Later history ==

By January 2008 the original ''dGamer'' site, dgamer.red84.com, was no longer available.<ref name="sf-18627-259468">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=259468#p259468 some IDEAS], Throdo, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (22 January 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261125174537/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t18627.html Internet Archive]</ref> Asked where the issues could be found, Angel Of Death said he had the first two; forum member Farmer Bob wrote that only three issues were ever made, one more than the short-lived [[Obi-Wan's Journal (newsletter)|Obi-Wan's Journal]], before the magazine became defunct.<ref name="sf-18627-259501">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=259501#p259501 some IDEAS], Farmer Bob, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (22 January 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261125174537/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t18627.html Internet Archive]</ref> The Players Committee's Advocate account answered that issue 3 was linked from the main PC website.<ref name="sf-18627-259504">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=259504#p259504 some IDEAS], Advocate, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums, forum.starwarsccg.org (22 January 2008). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261125174537/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t18627.html Internet Archive]</ref>
